verdict.touchpoint: Provider interface + getWhatsAppProvider factory (whatsapp-client.ts) — including the org-wide kill-switch override block
verdict.attackAttempted: Exploit the org-wide kill-switch (organizations.whatsapp_provider_override) against the product's PER-INSTANCE granularity. Scenario: An org runs a mix of Uazapi numbers AND meta_cloud numbers (the locked product decision). Once the proposal widens BOTH the override type cast (whatsapp-client.ts:207-211, proposal step 4) AND the DB CHECK on organizations.whatsapp_provider_override to include 'meta_cloud' (proposal step 6), the value 'meta_cloud' becomes a settable, HONORED org-wide override. The factory reads the override BEFORE instance.provider (lines 200-214) and coerces effectiveProvider for EVERY instance in that org. Set override='meta_cloud' (e.g. an admin/master flips the panic switch the wrong direction, or a future 'migrate this org to Meta' admin action reuses the same column): now getWhatsAppProvider() routes the org's perfectly healthy Uazapi instances into the meta_cloud branch — calling get_meta_cloud_credentials for a Uazapi instance (returns nothing -> throws) -> every Uazapi send for that org fails with provider_init_failed via whatsapp-dispatch.ts. The mirror case is just as bad and already shipped: the existing panic button override='uazapi' (its intended incident use) will now coerce that org's meta_cloud instances into the uazapi branch -> get_uazapi_credentials returns empty -> 'No uazapi credentials found' throw -> Meta numbers go dark. The override mechanism is org-scoped (single column on organizations) but the product is per-instance, so any override becomes an all-or-nothing hammer that breaks the OTHER provider's instances in mixed orgs.
verdict.notes: VERIFIED AGAINST REAL CODE. The factory branches themselves ARE isolated and additive (claim holds there): evolution-provider.ts and uazapi-provider.ts have hardcoded `readonly provider` literals, each factory if-block is byte-for-byte untouched, the unknown-provider throw at lines 275-277 stays loud, createInstance default at proxy line 216 stays 'uazapi'. The DB-CHECK/type-union lockstep risk is real but the proposal correctly calls it out. WHERE THE ISOLATION CLAIM ACTUALLY BREAKS is the layer ABOVE the branches — the kill-switch coercion (whatsapp-client.ts:200-214). The prior agent's mustFollowRules treat the override block as 'do not reorder, panic button, safe' but never reconcile its ORG-WIDE scope against the LOCKED per-instance product decision. Concrete impact on Uazapi (the thing being certified as unchanged): in a mixed org, setting whatsapp_provider_override='meta_cloud' coerces all Uazapi instances into the Meta branch and kills their sends; this is a NEW failure mode introduced purely by widening the override enum (proposal steps 4 + 6). Today (uazapi|evolution only) this same hammer exists but is harmless for the Uazapi-vs-Meta mix because 'meta_cloud' isn't a legal override value yet. Also note: the createInstance proxy block (whatsapp-api-proxy.ts:216-232) resolves provider ONLY from org override or hardcoded 'uazapi' default — it never reads payload.provider, so 'PER-INSTANCE provider selection at create time' is NOT actually wired; new meta_cloud instances cannot be created through the proxy as written. That is a functional gap, not a Uazapi regression, but it means the per-instance promise is currently unrealizable via the only entry point (whatsapp-api-proxy is the ONLY frontend path per its own header comment). Secondary: MassSend.tsx:68 filter `provider === 'uazapi'` correctly EXCLUDES meta_cloud (safe, as claimed); isFeatureUnavailable() string-matcher works for any provider (safe); inbound whatsapp-webhook is untouched and has no provider probe (safe). No RLS recursion, no shared mutable state beyond the per-org in-memory rate-limit map (which is provider-agnostic and unaffected).
verdict.breakDescription: The org-wide kill-switch override coerces ALL instances in an org to one provider, which collides with the locked PER-INSTANCE product decision. After widening the override enum to include 'meta_cloud' (proposal steps 4+6), an override value of 'meta_cloud' will route a mixed org's healthy Uazapi instances into the Meta branch (get_meta_cloud_credentials on a Uazapi instance -> throw -> all Uazapi sends fail), and the existing panic value 'uazapi' will conversely kill that org's Meta instances. Adding Meta therefore introduces a new, reachable way to break Uazapi behavior through this touchpoint. Separately, the createInstance path in whatsapp-api-proxy (lines 216-232) never reads a per-instance provider from the request — it only honors the org override or defaults to 'uazapi' — so per-instance Meta instances cannot actually be created via the documented sole entry point as the code stands.

verdict.breakDescription:
The literal claim 'zero code changes to whatsapp-webhook/index.ts' is true, but the broader isolation claim (uazapiImpact=none, systemImpact=low, no provider routing change needed) is FALSE. Two coupling vectors break Uazapi behavior the moment a meta_cloud row exists in whatsapp_instances:

VECTOR A — Type-union narrowing / missing default branch (CRITICAL): WhatsAppInstance.provider is typed 'evolution'|'uazapi' (whatsapp-client.ts:31, 177) and getWhatsAppProvider's `effectiveProvider` is typed 'uazapi'|'evolution' (line 200). When DB regen widens the column to include 'meta_cloud', the value flows in at runtime but matches neither the evolution nor uazapi branch, hitting `throw new Error('Unknown provider resolved=...')` (line 275). Every outbound path the webhook triggers (triggerReactions->sendTextViaInstance line 700; agent-message typing+reply; outbound-trigger; every other resolveDispatchContext caller) throws for that instance. CI has NO tsc gate (confirmed in CLAUDE.md), so the type widening provides zero compile-time protection.

VECTOR B — Shared org-wide instance selection (the real cross-provider pollution, NOT mitigated by isolation): The copilot reply path does NOT bind to the instance that received the inbound. agent-message:424-429 and whatsapp-dispatch.ts resolveInstance:124-136 pick 'first connected instance of the org' with no provider filter. In a mixed org, a Uazapi-inbound lead can have its AI reply attempted on the meta_cloud instance (and vice-versa). Even after getWhatsAppProvider learns meta_cloud, this sends the reply out the WRONG number / wrong channel — a silent mis-route, worse than a throw. The prior agent's mustFollowRules acknowledge getWhatsAppProvider must route meta_cloud, but the regressionRisks DISMISS this as 'mitigated by fail-safe in triggerReactions line 747 catches all errors'. That mitigation is wrong: (a) line 747 only guards the FALLBACK direct-call branch; the PRIMARY path is the queue insert (line 588), which succeeds, then the actual send happens later inside agent-message/copilot-batch-processor where there is no such webhook-local catch — agent-message:402-409 logs+rethrows; (b) 'errors caught + continues' means the lead gets NO copilot reply at all — that IS a Uazapi regression (today the Uazapi lead always gets answered).

So 'systemImpact=low / uazapiImpact=none' is incorrect: shipping the additive migration WITHOUT simultaneously (1) adding a meta_cloud branch to getWhatsAppProvider and (2) provider-scoping/channel-binding the org-wide instance selection will break copilot replies for Uazapi leads in any mixed org.

verdict.attackAttempted: Scoped the attack to the FULL proposedChange of this touchpoint, which explicitly includes its migration: "Requires single migration: ALTER whatsapp_instances provider CHECK constraint to add 'meta_cloud'." Scenario: an org adopts the locked PER-INSTANCE mixing decision (Uazapi + Meta numbers side by side). It already has a working Uazapi number. It connects a Meta Cloud number via Embedded Signup, creating a whatsapp_instances row with provider='meta_cloud'. Because instance creation order is not guaranteed (a Meta number connected during onboarding, or an org that starts on Meta and later adds Uazapi), the meta_cloud row can be the OLDEST row by created_at, OR simply carry status='connected'. Then I traced every outbound dispatch path that resolves an instance for that org.
verdict.notes:
THE BREAK (Uazapi outbound regression, triggered by THIS touchpoint's migration):

Shared resolver _shared/whatsapp-dispatch.ts:resolveInstance() (lines 107-138) selects the org instance with NO provider filter. Precedence is: preferred_instance_id, then "first instance of the org by created_at" (lines 124-129). The only optional filter is requireConnected -> status IN ('open','connected') (lines 131-134). It does NOT filter provider='uazapi'.

The moment the proposed migration widens the provider CHECK to allow 'meta_cloud' and an org has such a row, resolveInstance can return it for callers that send via Uazapi. The resolved row is passed to getWhatsAppProvider() in _shared/whatsapp-client.ts. That factory has exactly two branches ('evolution' line 219, 'uazapi' line 224) and a hard final `throw new Error("Unknown provider resolved=...")` at line 275-277. There is NO meta_cloud branch and NO default that routes/skips meta_cloud instances. resolveDispatchContext wraps this as DispatchResolutionError code 'provider_init_failed' (lines 218-226).

Net effect: for an org running BOTH providers, an existing, healthy Uazapi number stops sending — copilot replies, follow-ups, campaign/pipe dispatch, carteira bulk, portfolio-health nudges, schedule-meeting / transfer-human notifiers all fail — purely because a meta_cloud row was added. Uazapi behavior changes from "works" to "silently fails" with no Uazapi-side cause. This violates uazapiImpact=none and backwardCompatible=true.

Concrete worst path: _shared/outbound-sender.ts (the copilot turn) calls resolveDispatchContext with NO require_connected and NO preferred_instance_id when the agent has no bound instance (lines 87-92) -> falls straight to created_at-ordered first row -> meta_cloud -> throw -> copilot goes mute on the org's working Uazapi number. copilot-v2-worker (index.ts:160) uses requireConnected:true but is NOT saved: a Meta-connected number will carry status='connected' (same enum string Uazapi uses), so it passes the status filter and still throws.

Evidence the codebase KNOWS this filter is required elsewhere but the dispatch path omits it: whatsapp-health-monitor:130, whatsapp-rebind-webhook:127, whatsapp-session-watchdog:140 all do .eq("provider","uazapi"). The hot dispatch resolver does not.

SECONDARY (type-union narrowing, will hide the bug from the only safety net): WhatsAppInstance.provider is typed "evolution"|"uazapi" (whatsapp-client.ts:31) and WhatsAppProvider.provider is "evolution"|"uazapi" (line 177). After types.ts regen widens the DB enum, these hand-written shared types still narrow to the old union, so a meta_cloud row is silently mis-typed as uazapi at the type level. CI has NO tsc gate (per project gotchas: only eslint+depcruise+vite build), so this would not be caught in pipeline — it surfaces only at runtime as the "Unknown provider" throw.

TERTIARY (kill-switch can't rescue): organizations.whatsapp_provider_override CHECK (migration 20260423000200:13-14) only permits 'uazapi'|'evolution'. The factory override path (whatsapp-client.ts:200-217) can therefore never coerce a meta_cloud instance onto a sane provider. The panic button is blind to the third provider.

ON THE PRIOR AGENT'S SPECIFIC RULES (mostly fine, but their scope was too narrow):
- HMAC (line 52-56) is shared and validates all objects equally -> their rule holds; webhook-level signature is safe.
- Their rule "Use channel_messages only, not whatsapp_messages" is FACTUALLY WRONG for WhatsApp: the chat UI reads whatsapp_messages (useWhatsAppMessages.ts:41, useWhatsAppContacts.ts:59) and the Uazapi webhook writes whatsapp_messages (whatsapp-webhook/index.ts:708,837...). channel_messages is NOT what the WhatsApp chat renders. So Meta Cloud inbound written to channel_messages(channel='whatsapp') would be a silent functional dead-end (invisible in chat) — not a break of Uazapi, but the claim "current code unified all channels here" is false for the live WhatsApp surface.
- There IS an AFTER INSERT trigger on channel_messages (trg_meta_conv_upsert, migration 20261102000001:83-86). Its helper guards `IF p_channel NOT IN ('messenger','instagram') THEN RETURN` (line 19-21), so channel='whatsapp' rows are skipped -> no meta_conversations pollution. This trigger does NOT break, but the agent never mentioned it exists; writing channel='whatsapp' to a table carrying a meta-only trigger is fragile and should be called out.
- useIncomingMessageToast.ts subscribes to channel_messages INSERT but filters direction !== "inbound" (line 50), while channel_messages.direction CHECK only allows 'incoming'|'outgoing' (migration 20260717000000:38). So the toast is already dead for all channel_messages rows and will NOT fire on Meta Cloud either — benign, but proves the agent did not audit the realtime consumer it would feed.
- unified_inbox_messages view (migration 20260951100000:20) selects ALL channel_messages incl. channel='whatsapp'. Adding Meta Cloud whatsapp rows there is harmless dedup-wise (different external_ids) but means a WhatsApp conversation could appear twice in get_unified_conversations if both whatsapp_messages-derived and channel_messages-derived rows ever co-exist — worth a note, low severity.

UNIQUE-collision check (their regressionRisk #2): NO Uazapi collision risk on channel_messages, because Uazapi never writes channel_messages — it writes whatsapp_messages. The two tables are disjoint for WhatsApp today, so the UNIQUE(external_id,channel,organization_id) idempotency claim is fine for Meta Cloud in isolation.

BOTTOM LINE: The webhook code itself can be extended additively and safely (HMAC shared, third object branch, channel_messages write). But the migration the agent bundled into this touchpoint's proposedChange is NOT additive-only: it makes provider='meta_cloud' a legal value that an unfiltered, provider-agnostic dispatch resolver will hand to a factory with no meta_cloud branch and a hard throw, regressing live Uazapi outbound for any mixed org. classification should be 'requires-guard', not 'additive-only'; uazapiImpact is NOT none.

verdict.breakDescription:
The isolation claim scopes the change to the proxy touchpoint and asserts "Uazapi/Evolution instances continue routing to existing providers without modification." That is true ONLY for the proxy's own request path (which always carries an explicit instance_id). It is FALSE for the org-wide implicit resolver that reads the SAME table the proxy writes. Concretely:

1. PROXY IS THE WRITER. whatsapp-api-proxy/index.ts createInstance (lines 242-251) INSERTs the whatsapp_instances row and sets `provider`. The proposed change widens targetProvider to include 'meta_cloud'. Even though the proposal says "Meta instances are created externally via OAuth callback, not via this proxy," the row still lands in whatsapp_instances with provider='meta_cloud' — and that is the exact table the dispatch fleet reads.

2. NO PROVIDER FILTER IN IMPLICIT RESOLUTION. _shared/whatsapp-dispatch.ts resolveInstance() (lines 124-137) selects the org's instance by organization_id + optional status + created_at order + limit(1). There is literally no .eq('provider', ...) anywhere (grep for provider in whatsapp-dispatch.ts and instance-write-guard.ts returns ZERO matches). The same provider-blind pattern is duplicated inline in agent-message/index.ts:423-429 (sendTypingIndicator), campaign-rule-dispatch/index.ts:870-876, pipe-rule-dispatch:916, semi-automatic-dispatch:195, _shared/action-handlers/whatsapp-helpers.ts:52-61, _shared/actions/send-document.ts:288, copilot-v2-worker (resolveInstance requireConnected). This is ~8+ independent call sites.

3. RESULT: In a mixed org, a Uazapi-intended automation/copilot turn can silently resolve to the Meta instance. The MetaCloudProvider then either (a) throws on Uazapi-only paths (e.g. sendTypingIndicator setPresence, send-document, sendMenu — many of which are best-effort try/catch and would SILENTLY swallow), or (b) routes a free-form copilot reply through Meta's Cloud API where the 24h-window rule rejects non-template text → the lead's reply gets no answer, or the message is dropped, with the org believing their Uazapi number is healthy. This is a behavioral change to Uazapi-driven flows caused entirely by adding a Meta row to the shared table — i.e. the isolation claim is broken THROUGH the table the proxy mutates, even though the proxy's own dispatch switch is untouched.

4. SECONDARY (status semantics coupling). Implicit resolvers gate on status in ('open','connected'). 'open' is Evolution's connected marker, 'connected' is Uazapi's. A Meta instance must NOT reuse 'connected' as its live status, or it becomes indistinguishable from a live Uazapi number to every resolver. If it uses a NEW status (e.g. 'meta_active') it stays invisible to these resolvers (safe-ish) but then breaks the proxy's own createInstance status-write (line 291 writes literal 'connected'/'connecting') and the whatsapp-webhook status-mapper (maps to 'connected'). Either choice has a coupling consequence the proposal does not address.

The proposal's regression-risk #5 explicitly (and incorrectly) claims "Uazapi instances sending freeform text are NOT affected because factory correctly routes to UazapiProvider (line 269 provider.sendText)." That reasoning only covers the explicit-instance proxy path. It does not cover the implicit org-wide resolver, which is where the real cross-provider bleed happens.

NOTE: whatsapp-webhook inbound (the protected Uazapi path) is SAFE — it resolves instance strictly by id (whatsapp-helpers lines 161-167, 185-191; index.ts 661-664), so a Meta row cannot corrupt Uazapi inbound. The break is on the OUTBOUND/dispatch side via shared-table implicit resolution.

verdict.notes:
VERDICT: The isolation claim HOLDS for Uazapi through this touchpoint — I could not construct a path where adding meta_cloud changes Uazapi instance behavior. Evidence:

(A/B) FACTORY + NARROWING: whatsapp-client.ts:200 'let effectiveProvider: \"uazapi\"|\"evolution\" = instance.provider'. Widening instance.provider to add 'meta_cloud' makes this a tsc error, BUT: CI has NO tsc gate (only eslint+depcruise+vite build — confirmed in root CLAUDE.md gotchas + memory note project_ci_no_typecheck_gate). Deno edge runtime strips types entirely. So at RUNTIME a Uazapi instance still hits the `effectiveProvider === \"uazapi\"` branch (line 224) unchanged — Uazapi resolution is untouched. A meta_cloud instance with no MetaProvider branch falls to line-275 throw, which fails ONLY the meta_cloud caller, never a Uazapi one. Confirmed Uazapi isolation intact.

(C) MASS-SEND DOWNCAST — the real latent weakness, but NOT a Uazapi break: mass-send-create:142 passes `(instance as any).provider ?? \"uazapi\"` into decideDispatchRoute. The `as any` defeats the union widening entirely (Rule 3 is already violated by existing code). For a meta_cloud instance, decideDispatchRoute's `if (providerName !== \"uazapi\")` correctly returns custom_dispatcher → 400 'not eligible'. Safe by accident, not by type. The `?? \"uazapi\"` coercion is a footgun if provider is ever null, but defaulting to uazapi does not regress existing Uazapi sends.

(D) KILL-SWITCH: getWhatsAppProvider override block (lines 207-214) only accepts 'uazapi'|'evolution'. A meta_cloud instance under a stale 'uazapi' override would be coerced to Uazapi and throw on get_uazapi_credentials. This harms the meta_cloud path, never a Uazapi instance. whatsapp-api-proxy createInstance:216 has an identical narrow override cast — same conclusion.

(E) NO SHARED-STATE / CONSTRAINT / REALTIME COUPLING found: message-gateway.dispatchToProvider and whatsapp-dispatch send helpers are fully polymorphic (delegate to provider methods via factory, no provider-name branching). whatsapp-webhook (Uazapi inbound, 🔴) does NOT branch on the provider column (line 1127 explicitly notes 'no provider probe here'). The whatsapp_instances.provider CHECK ('evolution','uazapi') and organizations.whatsapp_provider_override CHECK ('uazapi','evolution') are independent column constraints — adding 'meta_cloud' to them does not alter any existing Uazapi row's validity. types.ts widens automatically on regen. No UNIQUE(message_id,instance_id) or realtime recursion implicated.

CONCLUSION: Uazapi behavior is NOT changed through this touchpoint by adding Meta as a third provider, PROVIDED the new code keeps Uazapi's branch first/unchanged and does not 'fix' the existing `as any` casts in a way that introduces a meta_cloud→uazapi coercion. The prior agent's classification (modified-risky, backwardCompatible=true, uazapiImpact=low) is accurate. systemImpact=medium is also fair because the meta_cloud path itself has real footguns. The proposed changes are sound but INCOMPLETE on enforcement — see extraRulesNeeded.
extraRulesNeeded: EXISTING `as any` CASTS DEFEAT THE UNION GUARANTEE: mass-send-create/index.ts:142 `(instance as any).provider ?? "uazapi"`, runUazapiSenderJob's `(provider as any).senderAdvanced` (dispatch-router:115), and whatsapp-api-proxy:216 narrow override cast all bypass tsc. Rule 1/Rule 3 (widen the literal union) provide ZERO compile-time protection at these exact call sites. Before adding meta_cloud, replace `(instance as any).provider ?? "uazapi"` with an explicit branch: if provider==='meta_cloud' return a 400/explicit reject — do NOT let `?? "uazapi"` silently coerce.

CI HAS NO tsc GATE (confirmed root CLAUDE.md + project_ci_no_typecheck_gate memory). Therefore Rule 1's premise ('forces tsc to flag missing cases') is FALSE in this repo's CI. Any exhaustiveness reliance must be backed by a unit test in whatsapp-adapter.test.ts asserting getWhatsAppProvider(meta_cloud_instance) returns MetaProvider AND a test asserting the factory throws (not silently returns) for an unknown provider. Add `tsc --noEmit` (or extend typecheck:ratchet to gate in CI) as part of this PR, or the union widening is cosmetic.

FACTORY ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING: keep the `effectiveProvider === "uazapi"` and `=== "evolution"` branches BYTE-IDENTICAL and BEFORE the meta_cloud branch. The line-275 `throw 'Unknown provider'` must remain a real throw (never a silent uazapi fallback) so a half-deployed meta_cloud (DB allows it, MetaProvider.ts not deployed) fails loudly on the meta_cloud instance instead of misrouting to Uazapi credentials.

KILL-SWITCH OVERRIDE MUST WIDEN IN BOTH PLACES OR NEITHER COERCES META: getWhatsAppProvider:207-214 AND whatsapp-api-proxy createInstance:216 both narrow-cast whatsapp_provider_override to ('uazapi'|'evolution'). If the CHECK constraint gains 'meta_cloud' but these casts stay narrow, a meta_cloud override is silently ignored / a meta_cloud instance under a stale override is coerced to uazapi. Widen all override-handling casts to three values atomically with the DB CHECK migration (Rule 6), or a meta_cloud instance can be force-routed to Uazapi credential lookup and throw.

DB-vs-CODE DEPLOY ORDER (hard sequencing): do NOT ship the migration adding 'meta_cloud' to whatsapp_instances.provider CHECK / organizations.whatsapp_provider_override CHECK until MetaProvider.ts is deployed in every edge function bundle that calls getWhatsAppProvider (whatsapp-api-proxy, message-gateway, dispatch-router callers, send-document, process-scheduled-user-messages, history-sync-worker, whatsapp-rebind-webhook). whatsapp-api-proxy:28-30 force-imports provider modules to include them in the eszip bundle — MetaProvider MUST be added to that force-import list or the dynamic import will be 'Module not found' at runtime (same class as the REALSC dynamic-import-not-in-eszip incident).

MassSend.tsx:68 `instances.filter((i) => i.provider === 'uazapi')` is a DEFAULT-DENY feature gate today (mass send is Uazapi /sender/* only). Keep it default-deny for meta_cloud: a meta_cloud instance must NOT appear in this list until a Meta-specific mass-send route exists, otherwise the user selects a meta_cloud instance and mass-send-create rejects with a confusing 400. Update the empty-state copy, not the filter semantics.

isFeatureUnavailable() matcher (useMessageActions.ts:101-108) matches 'does not support' / 'NotSupportedError' / 'only \"uazapi\" is supported'. MetaProvider MUST throw NotSupportedError (same string contract) for any Uazapi-only method Meta Cloud can't do (sendMenu, sendPixButton, react, edit, pin, deleteForAll, senderAdvanced, historySync, etc.). Do NOT change the matcher — it is a stable cross-provider contract; changing it can regress Evolution toasts too.

WhatsAppMigration.tsx:89 `(value as 'uazapi' | 'evolution')` override cast will go stale when a meta_cloud override option is added to the Select. No compile error will catch it (it's a cast). If a meta_cloud option is added to the dropdown UI without widening this cast, the value is silently mistyped. Widen this cast in lockstep with adding the UI option, or do not add the UI option.

CORE BREAK — instance resolution hijack in mixed orgs. _shared/whatsapp-dispatch.ts:124-137 resolveInstance() selects the org's earliest-created instance (ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT 1) with NO provider filter. requireConnected only filters status in ('open','connected'), not provider. This is NOT in the claim's regressionRisks. Uazapi's own code path is unchanged, but adding a Meta number breaks the shared dispatch layer the org relies on. systemImpact is at least medium, not 'low'.

The claim says 'no override for Meta' but the real risk is override targeting Uazapi clobbering Meta rows. Kill-switch must become provider-aware.
